entry.title: DIY Keyboard Update
entry.content:
This update took almost a year, and I wanted to explain why.

Over the summer, I did not think about the keyboard project much. When I came back to university in the fall, I started designing V2 with per-key LEDs. But I ended up making so many design changes that it took the entire fall semester and part of the spring semester just to get a PCB design that I believe might work. With coursework at the same time, I was not able to consistently work on the project over the past year.

What I am working on right now

1) V1.1 case revamp and mounting changes

I am currently working on a revamped version of the V1 case for V1.1. A major focus is the mounting method: this revision highlights a tray-mounting system instead of the gasket-over-tray approach I used in V1.

Here is an image representation of how the two mounting methods differ:

Gasket-over-tray mount (V1 style)

Tray mount (V1.1 direction)

Image source: MonsGeek - Comprehensive Guide to Keyboard Mounting Styles.

2) Knob circuit issue

As mentioned in the earlier project post, the knob circuit does not work right now because of a PCB design mistake. I am still iterating on this so the encoder support works properly in the updated revision.

3) Top cover redesign

I also updated the top-cover design with a more grid-like feature to better encase the switch-section zones.

More updates soon as I validate these hardware changes.

entry.title: DIY Keyboard V1
entry.content:
I finally finished my first custom keyboard build, and I am ridiculously proud of how it turned out. This is a 75 percent layout with a fully custom PCB, case, and firmware setup. It is my personal daily driver now, and it feels great to use something that I designed end to end.

What I built

This project, OP Keyboard, is a complete custom mechanical keyboard with a focus on usability and tweakability:

  • 75 percent layout that keeps function keys but stays compact
  • Custom PCB and case, both designed specifically for this board
  • Powered by a Raspberry Pi Pico
  • Two PCB build: a daughterboard (switchboard) and a main board that houses the dev board
  • Tray mount with a pin-connector socket between boards for reverse compatibility
  • QMK firmware for deep customization
  • VIA support for quick, on-the-fly remapping
  • A rotary encoder for media control or any macro you want
  • Open hardware files so it can be modified or remixed

Firmware and configurability

The firmware is built on QMK, which means it is as flexible as it gets. I can switch layers, remap keys, and change encoder behavior without rebuilding the whole setup. VIA support makes it even easier to experiment and dial in the perfect layout.

Current issues and fixes in progress

V1 is solid, but there are a couple things I want to improve:

  • The case is taller than I would like
  • Main board v1.0 does not support the rotary encoder because of a design mistake; I am working on a v1.1 to fix this

Links and project files

If you want to browse the project files, the repo is here:

  • https://github.com/SirAxolott/opkeyboard

What is next

This is V1, and I already have ideas for V2. The biggest upgrade will be per-key addressable RGB LEDs. I am also planning to write a full build guide soon, so keep an eye out if you want to make one yourself.
